digest.component_or_area: enrichment queue and ticket digest history management
propositions: Current queue/digest event reads are asymmetrically O(history): _events_of opens all matching files across 3 calls per ticket, totaling ~4,977 file opens and breaching the 20ms drain-gate budget; latest_ticket_digest is already O(1) with suffix-first reading
Physical deletion of committed UUID events provides no repository space reclamation (blobs remain in git history indefinitely) while breaking cross-clone merges via git rename-detection pairing

A merge-safe read-bound design using newest-first suffix scans with filename-prefix=event-timestamp reduces file opens to ≤3+k per ticket (at most 1-3 opens per event type) without deleting, renaming, or modifying any committed UUID events
The suffix-lazy reader design preserves invariant I1 (docs/concurrency.md) and cross-clone reconvergence by being read-only and deterministic across clones
Measured per-ticket event accumulation across 3,727 ticket dirs shows queue+digest events are only ~2% of working tree; the real cost driver is read frequency and listdir scaling, not storage size
The bounded read design is verified against the existing two-clone regression test and introduces no new deletion or rename of committed UUID events
